chunks: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — meaning al-Ridha — said to al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm: 'Which thing is al-Sakina in your view?' He said: 'I do not know, may I be your ransom, and what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A fragrant wind that comes out from Paradise, possessing a form like the face of a human being. It accompanies the Prophets, and it is that which descended upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he built the Kaaba — it began guiding thus and thus, and so he built the foundation upon it.'
[Second chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat]
He said: 'I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-Sakina, and he mentioned similar to it.'

key_terms.السَّكِينَة: al-Sakina — literally 'tranquility/serenity', a divine spiritual entity mentioned in the Quran (2:248, 9:26, 48:4) associated with divine presence and guidance for prophets
key_terms.الْأَسَاس: the foundation — the physical and divinely-guided groundwork of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: the Kaaba — the sacred cubic structure in Mecca, the qibla for Muslims, originally built by Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail (AS)
key_terms.رِيح: wind/breeze — here used to describe al-Sakina's physical manifestation as a moving entity from Paradise

ai.seo_question: What is al-Sakina according to Imam al-Ridha, and how did it guide Ibrahim in building the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) reveals to his companion al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm that al-Sakina — a term appearing multiple times in the Quran (e.g., 2:248, 9:26, 48:4) — is a fragrant wind from Paradise with a human-like face that accompanies the Prophets throughout history. The historical context is significant: al-Sakina had been debated among scholars, and the Imam provides an authoritative cosmological definition, specifically connecting it to the founding of the Kaaba, where it physically guided Ibrahim (AS) in laying the foundations of Islam's holiest site.
